title: SGS setting record: what each setting of one block changes
description: One block's record. An entry is one place a setting paints: the part, the CSS longhands, the state and the media conditions it holds under. check.py compares the record with a run of the block's code both ways; the key of an entry is (setting, part, props, state, tiers).

schemaVersion.description: 2 adds stamp, proofKeys, accounted and entry values; 1 is still read.

parts.description: The block's own part classes (sgs-<block>__<part>) the default render prints, in markup order.

setting.description: The block attribute (a fooUnit companion is folded into foo).

part.description: ROOT for the block root, else the part class (sgs-x__y), a bare tag under its classed ancestor (sgs-x__y svg), with ::before / ::after when the paint is on a pseudo-element. Classes of other blocks and shared helpers keep their own names.

props.description: CSS longhands, sorted; a shorthand stands for all of its longhands.

state.description: null at rest, else hover, focus, current, open, disabled, active, checked, filled (an input that holds a value: :not(:placeholder-shown)), or the selector token naming another state (a class token such as .is-detached is held by giving the element that class).

tiers.description: The at-rules the paint holds under (screen widths, forced colours, reduced motion); empty means always.

kind.description: value: the property takes the setting's value. switched-on: moving the setting off its default switches the declaration on, but its value is not the setting's. Required on every entry the check can see; an entry marked runner has none until the runner can see it.

runner.description: Set when the offline runner cannot see this paint yet (a render_block filter, wp_footer): the check lists the entry as skipped, never passes it silently. The value names the cause.

selector.description: The rule's selector, for people reading the record; never compared.

unproved.description: Set when the proof could not see what decides the entry, naming why. The entry is kept, but its kind is a reading, not a proof (switched-on for a true/false setting, else value): a reader that acts on kind must treat it as unproven.

values.description: The setting values whose renders produced this entry (the test values the check used).

symbolic.description: For a tier written from the setting's own value (a breakpoint setting): {edge, setting, offset}.

accepted.description: Set on an unproven entry whose shape (setting, element role, properties, state, media) is proved on another block and removed on none (accept.py): names those blocks. A reader may act on its kind.

proofKeys.description: The keys (setting, part, props, state, tiers) the plain comparison sees before the proof removes or re-files any, so check.py --no-proof is exact against this record.

stamp.description: What the record was checked against (stamp.py::make_stamp): inputs {file: hash}, outputs, theme, classes, tags.

accounted.description: Every setting not in an entry: tested with no paint, replacing the block, not valued (with the reason), or placed on a part the selector reader cannot name.

proofCache.description: One object per proofKeys entry, in the same order: what the proof found for it ('v': proved, blind, refiled or removed; 'kind'; 'cause'; 'to': the parts it was re-filed to) and 'fp', the fingerprint of everything that proof read (proof.py::Fingerprints). check.py reuses an outcome whose fingerprint still matches instead of proving the entry again.
